text:
Maya: customer reporting repeated 429s at ~2025-11-05T11:02:14Z even though the project quota tile showed ~3.9M tokens remaining for project `proj-acme-prod`. They provided APILog with request_id `r_9f3c2b` and timeline screenshots.

Kevin: can you drop project/org ids + one example request? I want raw meter events around the minute.

Maya: proj_id=proj_acme_prod, org_id=org_acme. Example APILog:
```
POST /v1/generate
request_id: r_9f3c2b
project: proj_acme_prod
tokens_consumed: 18600
status: 429 Too Many Requests
body: {"error": "quota exceeded"}
```

eng-sre-bot: collecting ingestion/ledger traces for proj_acme_prod between 2025-11-05T10:50:00Z and 2025-11-05T11:10:00Z

eng-sre-bot: preview: ledger_tokens_ingested=6,120,400 enforcement_count=3 last_enforcement_ts=2025-11-05T11:02:14Z dashboard_snapshot_ts=2025-11-05T11:02:00Z dashboard_tokens_left=3,902,600

Lina: odd — enforcement happened at 11:02:14Z but dashboard snapshot at 11:02:00Z shows tokens left. Sounds like a race where ledger had extra tokens that didn't make it into the UI snapshot.

Kevin: pulled raw ingestion events. Snippet (from ingestion topic):
```
2025-11-05T11:01:58.450Z event: token_emit project=proj_acme_prod tokens=1,120,000
2025-11-05T11:02:02.912Z event: token_emit project=proj_acme_prod tokens=1,480,000
2025-11-05T11:02:12.001Z event: token_emit project=proj_acme_prod tokens=3,520,000  <-- large worker batch
```

Kevin: timeline shows a ~3.52M batch that landed at 11:02:12Z and was processed by enforcement within ~2s, but our dashboard aggregator pulls micro-buckets that may be up to 5s stale depending on consumer lag. UI snapshot at 11:02:00Z didn't include the big batch but enforcement did once ledger committed.

Maya: customer saw first 429 at 11:02:14Z, consistent with enforcement seeing the large batch and crossing the limit. They want to know why the dashboard lied.

Sara: finance reconcile for org_acme 10:00-12:00Z shows total tokens=6,120,400 which matches ledger ingestion. No billing mismatch.

Lina: so billing correct; root cause is a visibility lag between micro-bucket-based UI snapshots and the ledger/enforcement path. We need to explain the race and offer mitigation.

Kevin: short-term mitigation: we can apply a temporary soft uplift for project `proj_acme_prod` while we fix the aggregator. Internal CLI: `rhq adjust-quota --project proj_acme_prod --soft-increase 12% --note "support: temporary uplift"` — I can run it now.

Kevin: executed at 2025-11-05T12:15:02Z — CLI output:
```
2025-11-05T12:15:02Z adjust-quota proj_acme_prod soft_increase=12% user=kevin
```

Maya: updated customer, they accepted the temporary uplift. Please make it visible in the support ticket.

Lina: proposed long-term fixes:
- When rendering dashboard tiles, rehydrate the last-second ledger tail (last N events or last 10s) to eliminate undercount races.
- Reduce micro-bucket consumer poll interval from 2s -> 300ms for high-volume projects.
- Emit a monitoring metric: ui_snapshot_delay = ledger_latest_ts - dashboard_snapshot_ts; alert if > 2s for any project.

Kevin: created INF-2486: "UI snapshot undercounts when ingestion bursts arrive between micro-bucket boundaries -> enforcement mismatch". Assigned to eng-metrics, priority P1 for visibility bug. Attached ingestion traces and sample APILog.

eng-sre-bot: rollout suggestion: (A) dashboard rehydration patch -> patch release to staging 2025-11-06, canary 2025-11-07, full roll 2025-11-09; (B) monitoring alert rule added immediately.

Sara: finance confirms no invoicing action needed; noted uplift in support log to be reverted after fix/confirmation.

Maya: final message to customer: apologized, explained race between UI and enforcement, noted temporary +12% soft-limit applied, promised a fix timeline (ETA 2025-11-09) and will follow up when the dashboard shows consistent numbers. Customer replied they appreciate the quick uplift and will monitor.

Kevin: marking support thread resolved pending ENG fix. I'll update INF-2486 with canary results and close once metrics show ui_snapshot_delay < 500ms for 24h.

Lina: assigning follow-up to eng-metrics and tagging @lina in INF-2486.

Maya: closing thread — will reopen if customer sees more 429s. :pray:
